prerequisites: Familiarity with the use of a symbolic computation package

learning_outcomes.text: Students will have an overview of applications of partial differential equations in various engineering disciplines. For a number of model problems (temperature profile in a thin rod or long cylinder, temperature distribution in a thin plate, vibration of a string or elastic membrane, transport,...), they can formulate and interpret the differential equations and associated initial and/or boundary conditions.

Students understand how the method of separation of variables and the method of characteristic curves work for solving partial differential equations and can assess their applicability. They can apply the methods to a number of model problems, working out the results with pen and paper and using a symbolic computation package. They can interpret and visualize the results. They know the properties of solutions of different types of equations.
Students know and understand the properties of the Laplace transform and can apply this transform to solve differential equations.

syllabus_topics: Method of separation of variables applied to the one-dimensional wave and heat equation and the Laplace equation
Cylinder-symmetric problems, temperature profile in a long cylinder, temperature distribution in a solid cylinder and a circular disc
Method of characteristic curves (derivation, transport equation, damped transport equation, non-linear transport equations and shock waves, wave equation)
Laplace transform (definition, properties, convolution, gamma function, inverse transform, solving differential equations)
teaching_methods: Practical exercises (pen and paper, symbolic computation package)

assessment_methods.method: Exam during the examination period - exercises (open book on PC) for Partial Differential Equations and Fourier Series
Exam during the examination period - theory and/or exercises with pen and paper (closed book with formula sheet) for Transformations

assessment_rules: The exam consists of two parts. Part 1 covers exercises on Partial Differential Equations and Fourier Series (up to Section 4.3 "Cylinder-symmetric problems"), which is open book and allows the use of a PC with sample programs. Part 2 covers theory and/or exercises on Transformations (from Section 4.4 "Method of Characteristic Curves"), which is a closed book exam where a formula sheet is permitted.
institution: KU Leuven - Faculty of Engineering Science
degree: Bachelor in de ingenieurswetenschappen (Bachelor of Engineering Science, Leuven)
